title: SLO stakeholder onramp checklist and simulation scripts
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, actionable onramp for service owners and partner teams to: (1) align SLO goals, error budget policies, and handoff requirements; (2) run lightweight failure/simulation scripts that validate monitoring and rollback pathways; and (3) carry out a short safe-canary so teams can graduate to a monitored SLO.

Why this exists (context):
- We repeatedly see flaky monitoring/alerting surface only after an SLO goes live — expensive firefights across eng, product, and infra.
- Need a standard, low-friction way for service teams to validate the whole stack (metrics, dashboards, alert routing, incident playbooks, operator permissions) before an SLO is accepted.
- This is an "onramp" not a heavy process: 1–2 week lightweight experiment with explicit simulation steps and clear rollback triggers.

Scope / Non‑scope:
- Scope: model-serving endpoints, API gateway frontends, and routing layers that directly impact hosted inference latency and error rates.
- Non-scope: internal tooling dashboards, batch jobs, and third-party integrations without SLO impact.

Success criteria (how we know this worked):
- Observability validated end-to-end: alerts fire to expected pager/Slack channel during scripted failures.
- Canary run stays within agreed error budget for 48 hours OR triggers automatic rollback per policy.
- Post-onramp retro lists <3 actionable gaps (monitoring, runbooks, permissions) to close.
- Service added to SLO roster and SLO dashboard with owner assigned.

Stakeholders & roles (one-line):
- SLO Owner: service/product lead (responsible for target, business impact classification).
- SRE Sponsor: oncall/team SRE (validates instrumentation, runbook quality).
- Observability Eng: dashboard + alert delivery (configures dashboards, alert routing).
- Platform Ops: canary infra & rollback toggles (flip/observe traffic routing).
- Incident Commander backup: product or TPM for high-impact customer channels.

High-level timeline (typical 7–14 days):
1) Day 0: Kickoff sync (30m) — align target SLOs, risk appetite, and onramp dates.
2) Day 1–2: Instrumentation audit + quick fixes (metrics, traces, synthetic checks).
3) Day 3–5: Simulation scripts run in staging, alert routing verification.
4) Day 6: Dry-run canary (0–5% traffic) with SRE observing.
5) Day 7–10: Extended canary (10–25% traffic) or stop early if rollback triggers.
6) Day 10–14: Retro, document gaps, sign-off to add to SLO dashboard.

Checklist: pre-run (SLO Owner)
- [ ] Document SLO target, burn-rate policy, and business impact (P0/P1).
- [ ] Confirm owner and SRE sponsor + backup.
- [ ] Link runbook draft and alert contact lists.
- [ ] Ensure metrics exist (request_latency_p50/p95, request_error_rate, synthetic-health-check).
- [ ] Verify metric retention/aggregation windows align with SLO window.
- [ ] Confirm platform toggles for canary (traffic weight controls, feature flags).

Checklist: pre-run (SRE Sponsor / Observability)
- [ ] Create dashboard with SLO widget and burn-rate alert.
- [ ] Configure alert routing (pager, Slack, mailing list) and escalation policy.
- [ ] Add playbook link to alert body.
- [ ] Set a blue/green rollback plan + owner who can flip traffic.

Simulation scripts (quick-run examples):
- Purpose: validate that (a) metrics increment as expected, (b) alerts fire and route, (c) rollback path works.
- Run these in staging first; each script includes a verification step.

1) latency-spike.sh (bash) — simulates CPU/latency slowness- Steps: curl synthetic endpoint with injected sleep header 1000x; verify p95 rises by configured margin; expect burn-rate alert to trigger at step threshold.- Verification: observe synthetic check and traces surface increased tail latency; confirm alert delivered.

2) error-flood.py (python) — simulates 500s for a portion of requests- Steps: send batched requests with error-forcing header to 10% of hits for 5 minutes.- Verification: request_error_rate rises; on-call receives page; runbook executed (ack + mitigation).

3) dependency-failover.sim (k6 or locust script) — partially fail downstream cache/db- Steps: toggle feature-proxy to force fallback path, or use a chaos stub to inject timeouts to downstream.- Verification: traces show dependency errors, fallback path exercised, SLI delta recorded.

Canary & rollback policy (decision thresholds):
- Automatic rollback: if burn rate >= 6x AND SLI breach persists > 10 minutes, platform ops flips canary to 0% (or triggers circuit-breaker).
- Manual rollback: SRE Sponsor or SLO Owner can request rollback at any sign of customer-impacting regression.
- Emergency escalation: if customer-reported incidents exceed threshold (>=3 P1s in 1 hour), IC to convene auto-rollback.

Metrics to capture during the run (minimum):
- SLI time-series (p50/p95/p99 latency), request_error_rate, synthetic_health, avg_burn_rate
- Alert firing timestamps and delivery path (Slack msg id, pager id)
- Rollback action timestamp and actor id

Risk heatmap (short):
- Observability gaps: medium — likely to miss an alert destination. Mitigation: pre-run verification and manual paging test.
- Runbook quality: medium-high — untested runbooks cause delays. Mitigation: tabletop dry run.
- Traffic control errors: low — platform has safe toggles, but test nevertheless.

Communication plan (during canary):
- Slack channel: #sre-onramp-<service> (create ephemeral channel for the run).
- 15m check-ins during canary windows with SRE Sponsor and Platform Ops.
- Update status doc (single-line updates) every 2 hours during active canary.

Post-run retro template (to fill):
- What worked?
- What surprised us?
- Monitoring gaps found (list + owners)
- Runbook updates required (Y/N)
- Action items (owner + due date)

Open questions / decisions to make before Day 0:
- Burn-rate multiple for this class of service (suggest 4x for low-risk, 6x for public facing).
- SLO window length to use: 7d vs 28d for p99-sensitive endpoints.
- Which dashboards get promoted to long-term retention for trend analysis?

Next steps (recommended immediate actions):
- Owner book kickoff (30m) with SRE Sponsor and Observability within 72h.
- Tech lead populate instrumentation checklist and attach to this doc.
- Observability Eng to create the alert + dashboard template (link in linked_artifacts).
- Platform Ops to verify canary toggle exists (PR if not).

Notes to self / scratchpad (informal):
- Keep canary small first — too many variables blow up root cause.
- If platform rollback takes >5m, escalate to infra oncall.
- Consider adding a short synthetic that exercises multi-region routing for geo failover tests.

Appendix: quick run commands (staging):
- latency-spike.sh: for i in {1..1000}; do curl -H 'X-Debug-Sleep:1000' https://staging.service/synthetic; done
- error-flood.py: python3 scripts/error_flood.py --percent 10 --duration 300 --url https://staging.service/api/endpoint
- verify-alerts.md: steps to check Slack/pager delivery (link to Observability playbook).

If you own a service and want to run this onramp, ping @priya (SRE sponsor) or open REL-3123 and we'll assign the next available slot.

-- end of doc --
